title: Migration kit and grace-period policy for API behavior changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a bundled Migration Kit and a formalized grace-period policy for changes to core API behavior (streaming semantics, function/tool-calling contracts, and structured output formats). The kit should make it straightforward for customers to adopt new defaults or pin older behavior via behavior flags, SDK helpers, and migration guides. The policy must define timelines (preview, opt-in, deprecation warning, enforced switch), observability requirements, and an automated backward-compatibility test suite to catch regressions across SDKs and model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide published that covers: streaming edge-cases, function/tool-calling schema changes, and structured-output schema evolution
SDK patch helpers (node/python/go) that expose behavior flags and a compatibility shim to keep older semantics when requested
Grace-period policy documented with clear timelines: 30d preview, 90d opt-in, 180d deprecation window (typical), and emergency rollback steps
Automated BCT (backward-compatibility test) jobs are in CI and run nightly against maintained SDKs and model compatibility matrix
Canary rollout playbook for runtime changes that might affect latency/streaming behavior and a tracing dashboard to evaluate impact
Customer-facing deprecation emails template and in-console banners that can be toggled per org
updates: 2026-02-20 - Kickoff: scoped deliverables with Eng and DX. Agreed to prioritize SDK helpers and automated tests ahead of docs.
2026-02-26 - Eng design review: decided to implement behavior flags as HTTP headers and SDK-level toggles; runtime will accept both for backwards compatibility.
2026-03-02 - PM + Legal: finalized deprecation timeline template and minimum notice windows for enterprise customers (extendable via support SLA).

2026-03-05 - Eng prototype: initial compatibility shim PR created (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128). Prototype supports: streaming chunk framing differences, function-call name normalization, and lenient structured-output parsing.
2026-03-10 - Design review: UX microcopy for console banners and migration flow approved (Figma: redwood.design/file/console-migration-2026).
notes: Decision: Behavior flags will be first-class and exposed via: HTTP header 'X-Redwood-Compat' (comma-separated tokens) and SDK config option 'compat:'
Trade-off: Header-based approach keeps runtime routing simple but requires clients behind CDNs/proxies to pass headers explicitly; SDKs will automatically set headers where possible.

Edge-case: For streaming changes, we will support per-request header and client-initiated session setting; persistent org-level toggles require console feature flag support (to be negotiated with infra).
Regulatory: Private deployments can opt for extended deprecation windows and offline patch bundles; include a checklist in the migration guide.
migration_steps: Publish migration guide and sample scripts that detect breaking usages (e.g., relying on implicit tokenization or positional tool-call ordering)
Release SDK helpers v0.1 (node, python, go) exposing 'compat' API and automatically wiring HTTP headers
Run migration-lint job on top customers' anonymized request traces to surface likely impacted prompt patterns (opt-in)
Open deprecation timeline for the first change (structured-output ontology update) with 90d opt-in window
Coordinate canary rollout: 1% traffic for 2 weeks, 5% next 2 weeks, with rollback gates tied to error/latency thresholds
testing_plan: Nightly BCT: run canonical prompts through latest runtime against all maintained SDK versions; fail build on semantic diffs beyond threshold
Golden files for streaming outputs: validate chunk boundaries and end-of-stream markers across model variants
Function-call contract tests: validate name/value normalization and fallback behavior when parameters are missing
Structured-output schema fuzzing: generate mutants of expected schema and assert graceful parsing/backward-tolerant behavior
Load test for compatibility shim to measure added latency at P50/P95 to ensure SLOs aren't violated
rollback_plan: Immediate: flip org-level console banner to force 'legacy' behavior for affected orgs
Short-term: runtime toggle to route affected traffic to previous stable binary build for up to 72 hours
Long-term: hotfix patch in runtime and SDK helpers with a follow-up compatibility release and extended customer comms
